dedupe_keys.name: global solid waste generation and warming equivalent emission scenarios to 2050 science 2023 data

description: These workbooks project how much solid waste the world will generate to 2050 and how much warming its methane, carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide will cause under different ways of managing it. The producers are Zheng Xuan Hoy, Kok Sin Woon and Wen Cheong Chin of Xiamen University Malaysia, Yee Van Fan of Brno University of Technology and Seung Jick Yoo of Sookmyung Women's University, and the data support their 2023 Science article on curbing waste emissions toward net-zero warming. Coverage is global, with waste generation estimated at 2.56 to 3.33 billion tonnes by 2050 and scenarios of technical and behavioural change that could make the waste system net-zero in warming terms relative to 2020 if adopted by 2033 to 2041. The two supplementary workbooks and a readme are available as a free download from Dryad and a Zenodo copy under a CC0 public domain dedication. Caveats: aggregated projections that depend on scenario assumptions, and the method and variable definitions sit in the article, not the files. Simulation uses: setting long-term waste treatment and emission pathways for climate mitigation planning and testing landfill methane policies. Related records: the Global Waste Sector Dataset (data-global-waste-sector-1990-2050) from the same group gives national series, and LandGEM (model-landgem) estimates landfill gas.
